Playbook.name: Windows — Execution via MS VisualStudio Pre/Post Build Events - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: MSBuild.exe spawned cmd.exe running a build-event temp script (tmp*.exec.cmd) - pre/post-build events can be abused to run arbitrary code under a trusted developer tool. Triage question: is this abuse of MSBuild for execution, or a legitimate software build?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: MSBuild build-event execution proxies code under a signed developer utility, useful for allowlist bypass and living-off-the-land on dev machines.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the MSBuild build-event execution is abuse or a legitimate build.

Step.name: MSBuild child command and context
Step.Purpose: The build-event command and whether this host is a developer machine separate abuse from normal builds.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.parent.name RLIKE "(?i)msbuild(.exe)?" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: On a developer workstation, MSBuild build events are normal. On a server/non-dev host, MSBuild spawning cmd from a temp exec.cmd is suspicious. The command content and host role are the discriminators.

Step.name: Process origin and account on the host
Step.Purpose: The parent process and account reveal whether this was interactive attacker activity or an automated/service context.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS runs = COUNT(*), parents = VALUES(process.parent.name), users = VALUES(user.name) BY process.name | SORT runs DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A suspicious process spawned by an office app/browser/script interpreter, run by a normal user, is more concerning than one under a known admin/automation parent.

Node.Condition: MSBuild build-event execution on a non-developer host, or a suspicious build-event command.
A legitimate software build on a developer workstation/build server.
MSBuild execution with unclear host role/command.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-MSBUILD-CHILD, INV-02-PROC-TREE to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A legitimate build on a dev/build machine.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the build context; close as benign_activity.

TruePositive.Definition: Abuse of MSBuild for code execution.

SOCAction.Item: Investigate the host/account; open IR if malicious.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A CI/CD agent building on a server by design.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
